findings.documented: Timestamps are ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix, everywhere in the API
findings.actual: Health clock uses an explicit IST offset, e.g. 2026-09-14T22:55:13.642242+05:30
findings.how_found: Called GET /health with no authentication and checked server_time format
findings.impact: Any client code that assumes UTC 'Z' suffix shifts dates by 5.5 hours, breaking 7-day interval calculations

findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key as a query parameter ?api_key=
findings.actual: The API rejects query-parameter keys (401: {"detail":"send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter"}) and requires the X-API-Key request header instead
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/listings?api_key=... and compared with header X-API-Key: ...

findings.documented: POST /auth/login returns { token, token_type, expires_in: 86400, user }. Tokens valid for 24 hours with no refresh flow.
findings.actual: Response returns 'access_token' (not 'token'), expires_in=900 (15 minutes, not 24 hours), and provides refresh_token and refresh_url
findings.how_found: Logged in via POST /auth/login with demo credentials and inspected response envelope
findings.impact: Clients expecting token field fail to authenticate; tokens expire after 15 minutes unless refreshed

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings
findings.impact: Comparable property widgets cannot query this endpoint and must filter listings locally

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites, and DELETE /v1/favourites/{id} manage server-side user favourites
findings.actual: All favourites endpoints return 404 Not Found
findings.how_found: Tested GET, POST, and DELETE on /v1/favourites
findings.impact: Favourites cannot be stored on the remote API; the application must persist them in local database or localStorage

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregates for your city
findings.impact: Insights screen must compute aggregations client-side or via backend worker

findings.documented: Collection endpoints take page + limit (maximum 200) and return { total, page, page_size, results }
findings.actual: Responses use offset-based pagination { limit: 50, offset, count, total, has_more, results }. Server caps limit at 50 even when limit=100/200 is requested.
findings.how_found: Probed GET /v1/listings with limit=100 and limit=200; inspected echoed limit and results count
findings.impact: A client assuming limit=200 under-fetches records; must use offset pagination with step 50

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings returns active sale listings only; inactive, expired and withdrawn are excluded server-side
findings.actual: Retrievable records include 878 listings where is_live === false (out of 4200 total)
findings.how_found: Paged through all listings and inspected is_live boolean field
findings.impact: Catalogue screens must explicitly filter by is_live === true to prevent showing expired/withdrawn properties

findings.documented: Area: Square feet, integer, everywhere in the API
findings.actual: 305 listings report carpet_area in square metres (sqm), e.g. 70-150 for 2-3 BHKs, rather than square feet
findings.how_found: Inspected carpet_area distribution across 2+ BHK listings
findings.impact: Price per square foot calculations and area filters are distorted by a factor of 10.76 if unnormalized

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in integer rupees
findings.actual: Project price fields are stored as decimal floats in Lakhs (< 100) and Crores (< 10), e.g. Casagrand Willows price_min=72.4 (Lakhs) and price_max=1.08 (Crores), not raw integer INR
findings.how_found: Inspected project.price_min and project.price_max values across all 450 projects
findings.impact: Displaying project prices as raw rupees renders ₹72 instead of ₹72,40,000

findings.documented: Each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property
findings.actual: 357 physical properties are listed multiple times across different portals (e.g. Zerobroker, Squarelane, Magichomes) with matching building, floor, bedroom, and coordinates
findings.how_found: Grouped listings by (apartment_name, locality, floor, bedroom) and confirmed matching GPS and facing direction
findings.impact: Naively treating each listing record as a distinct property overcounts city inventory by ~9.8%

findings.documented: Listing records represent valid physical real estate properties
findings.actual: 38 listing records contain physically impossible attributes (e.g. negative prices, carpet area > super built-up, floor > total floors)
findings.how_found: Audited physical invariants across all retrievable listings
findings.impact: Must be excluded from price metrics and hidden from catalog displays

findings.documented: All listings are genuine sale listings
findings.actual: 9 listings identified as fake/enquiry bait designed to harvest leads
findings.how_found: Audited listing flags, extreme price-per-square-foot ratios, and enquiry-bait descriptions
findings.impact: Distorts inventory counts and average price benchmarks if not filtered out

findings.documented: total_listings always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns
findings.actual: For project P20001, total_listings=1, actual retrievable listings=9, and filtering by project_id returned 10 rows
findings.how_found: Compared project.total_listings to listings dataset count and tested GET /v1/listings?project_id=...
findings.impact: UI cards cannot trust project.total_listings or the project_id query filter

findings.documented: total_listings is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with retrievable listings
findings.actual: 354 projects report a total_listings that differs from the actual count of retrievable listings with that project_id
findings.how_found: Grouped listings by project_id and compared counts with project.total_listings
findings.impact: Project inventory numbers reported in project cards are inconsistent with retrievable listings
